newsitem.title: USA: Firm prices for foreign crudes lift U.S. domestics.
newsitem.headline: Firm prices for foreign crudes lift U.S. domestics.

text.p: Firmer prices for foreign crudes, an evaporating WTI-Brent spread and other supply factors all aided a push to stronger differentials for domestic grades on Thursday in the U.S. Gulf, traders said.

At the same time grades gained, outright prices lost steam to end down for the session. September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing talked late Thursday at $20.05-15 a barrel, 10 cents weaker than Wednesday.
Outrights fluctuated with the NYMEX screen, where early session gains evaporated over the course of the day. Most traders said deflating unleaded gasoline prices hit crude.
Sweet grade barrels benefitted from more expensive foreign crudes in the Gulf. Dated Brent also gained ground, bolstered by lower-than-expected North Sea loading programs.
"The WTI-Brent spread really caved in, so that pushed at the LLS, too," said a trader.

September Brent-WTI moved below $1.00 to 90 cents at the time of the NYMEX settlement. North Sea Brent was notionally assessed at October WTI/Cushing even to minus five cents a barrel for one million barrels delivered into the Gulf.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James gained nearly 10 cents from the differentials on Wednesday, selling to 27 cents over the marker, but talked late at 22-24 cents over.
Midland/WTI stuck at WTI -30/28 cents, and Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire at -32 cents to September WTI.
West Texas Sour/Midland sold to $1.30 under WTI, and Eugene Island was widely discussed at WTI -$1.40/30.
WTI/Cushing Postings Plus was at $1.84-88, a shade stronger than Wednesday, but within yesterday's trading band.
News in the market had Iraq gaining approval for two more contracts, bringing the total to 16 contracts approved for 83.52 million barrels under the U.N. "oil-for-food" accord.

Mobil said earlier Thursday that it will buy 3.6 million barrels of Iraqi crude over the span of the June to December oil deal. Mobil makes the fourth U.S. firm to take Iraqi crude, with Chevron, Coastal and Bayoil.
